scenes.heading: Pricing yourself: commission splits, fees, and what agents actually take home

sents.d: Pricing yourself: commission splits, fees, and what agents actually take home
Understanding the full cost structure prevents surprises at your first closing.

Commission is typically split between the buyer's and seller's agents, then each agent splits their portion with their brokerage — meaning the advertised total commission rate is significantly more than what any individual agent actually takes home.

Brokerage splits vary (a common range might be 50/50 for newer agents, improving over time or with production), and many brokerages also charge desk fees, technology fees, or transaction fees on top of the split.

Understanding your realistic take-home per closed deal — not just the headline commission percentage — is essential for setting income expectations and deciding how many transactions you actually need to close to reach a target income.

take: Calculate your real take-home per deal, not the headline rate.
